pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the walled city lies pale and gold across the middle distance under a wide luminous evening sky, its domes and towers ringed by bare hills, while the olive slopes of the foreground fall away in grey green terraces where small robed figures rest beside kneeling camels, as they approached jerusalem and came to bethphage and bethany at the mount of olives, jesus sent out two of his disciples, and said to them, go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat, untie it and bring it here
pictures.name: pd_church_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Pieter de Hooch, The Courtyard of a House in Delft — a woman in a dark bodice and a white cap leads a small girl by the hand down two worn steps into a swept brick courtyard, a red brick archway with a carved stone tablet set above it standing beside them and a long shadowed passage opening past a doorway to the sunlit street beyond, if anyone asks, why are you doing this, tell him, the lord needs it and will return it shortly, so they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway, they untied it
pictures.name: pd_de_hooch_courtyard_of_a_house_in_delft

pictures.scene: Andrei Ryabushkin, A Moscow Street on a Holiday — a young woman in a long red coat of pearl buttons and a white embroidered headcloth picks her way along a road of wet planks and puddles, a bearded man in a tall black fur hat and a gold patterned caftan riding up behind her and others seated by a painted icon shrine watching her pass, and some who were standing there asked, why are you untying the colt, the disciples answered as jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission
pictures.name: pd_ryabushkin_moscow_street_holiday

pictures.scene: Constant Troyon, On the Way to the Market — a woman in a brown cloak rides side saddle on a grey donkey down a misty autumn road at first light, a drover in a broad hat following behind her and a press of sheep, cattle and a white dog crowding the lane on every side under tall half bare trees, then they led the colt to jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and he sat on it, many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields
pictures.name: pd_troyon_on_the_way_to_the_market

pictures.scene: Gentile Bellini, Procession in Piazza San Marco — a long procession crosses the wide pink pavement of the square before the gold mosaics and grey domes of the basilica, white robed brothers carrying tall candles and a gilded reliquary under a red and gold canopy while ranks of dignitaries in scarlet and black stand watching on either side, the ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting, hosanna, blessed is he who comes in the name of the lord, blessed is the coming kingdom of our father david, hosanna in the highest
pictures.name: pd_bellini_procession_piazza_san_marco

pictures.scene: Max Liebermann, The Twelve Year Old Jesus in the Temple — a sandalled boy in a plain pale robe stands small in the middle of a circle of bearded elders in prayer shawls and dark coats, one seated old man bending close to answer Him and the others pressing in around the reading desk of the dim temple hall to argue and listen, then jesus entered jerusalem and went into the temple courts, he looked around at everything, but since it was already late, he went out to bethany with the twelve, the next day, when they had left bethany, jesus was hungry
pictures.name: pd_liebermann_jesus_im_tempel

pictures.scene: Camille Pissarro, Orchard in Bloom at Louveciennes — a single fruit tree stands in the middle of a ploughed orchard with its whole crown thick in white blossom and new green leaf against a pale blue sky, a stooping figure in a blue smock working at a heap of cut branches on the bare brown earth behind it, seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, he went to see if there was any fruit on it, but when he reached it, he found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs, then he said to the tree, may no one ever eat of your fruit again, and his disciples heard this statement
pictures.name: pd_pissarro_orchard_in_bloom_louveciennes

pictures.scene: Marinus van Reymerswaele, A Moneychanger and His Wife — a money changer in a great scarlet turban leans over his balance with his thin hand poised on the beam while his wife in a white headcloth and a rose gown bends in beside him to watch, the dark table before them covered with heaped stacks of gold and silver coin, a weighing box and an open ledger, when they arrived in jerusalem, jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there, he overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves, and he would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts
pictures.name: pd_van_reymerswaele_a_moneychanger_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Emanuel de Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — white gothic piers and tall traceried windows rise over a packed wooden pew enclosure where a preacher leans out of the high pulpit with his hand put forward, hatted listeners seated close below him and a woman with two children and a spaniel standing in the sunlit aisle in the foreground, then jesus began to teach them, and he declared, is it not written, my house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations, but you have made it a den of robbers, when the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill him, for they were afraid of him, because the whole crowd was astonished at his teaching
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk_amsterdam_during_a_sermon

pictures.scene: Charles Leickert, The Town Gate — townsfolk in white caps and dark bodices stand talking on the cobbles before a stepped gable gatehouse at the end of the street, one woman balancing a basket on her head and a boy kneeling over a pail beside her, while under the deep brick archway a bright market square crowded with small figures opens out beyond the town, and when evening came, jesus and his disciples went out of the city, as they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots
pictures.name: pd_leickert_poort

pictures.scene: Mihaly Munkacsy, Woman Carrying Brushwood — a young woman in a red cap, a white shirt and a blue grey apron has sat down on a stony bank at the edge of a dark wood to rest, a great bundle of dry broken sticks still strapped across her back and her face bent low over her folded arms, peter remembered it and said, look, rabbi, the fig tree you cursed has withered, have faith in god, jesus said to them
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_vrouw_met_takkenbos

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Chalk Cliffs on Rugen — white spires of chalk frame a gap that opens straight down onto a wide still sea with two small sails far out on it, green beech branches arching overhead and three walkers at the brink, a woman in a red dress pointing down into the chasm and a man on his hands and knees peering over the edge, truly i tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, be lifted up and thrown into the sea, and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him, therefore i tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_chalk_cliffs_on_rugen

pictures.scene: Jan Victors, Hannah Praying in the Temple — an older woman in a broad red pleated hat, a fur lined mantle and a white ruffed collar stands before a stone pillar with her worn hands tightly clasped at her breast, her lined face lifted and her lips parted as she prays in the shadow of the temple porch, and when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well, after their return to jerusalem, jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to him
pictures.name: pd_victors_hanna_biddend_in_de_tempel

pictures.scene: Albrecht Durer, Christ among the Doctors — a long haired boy in a blue green robe stands in the middle of a tight ring of scholars with His hands raised before Him, counting the argument off on His fingers, an old man with a jutting toothless jaw pressing in at His shoulder to answer and the others crowding close with open books held up on every side, by what authority are you doing these things, they asked, and who gave you the authority to do them, i will ask you one question, jesus replied, and if you answer me, i will tell you by what authority i am doing these things
pictures.name: pd_durer_doctors

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — a huge crowd of country people in hoods, straw hats and white kerchiefs sits and stands packed together on a wooded slope, a few perched up among the branches overhead, every face turned toward a gaunt preacher in a brown robe who stands among them with his arms spread wide, john's baptism, was it from heaven or from men, answer me, they deliberated among themselves what they should answer, if we say, from heaven, he will ask, why then did you not believe him
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Dirck van Delen, The Pharisee and the Publican — a tall pale church arcade of clustered columns and high vaults stretches away over a blue and cream chequered floor, a barefoot man in a wine red mantle standing at a pier with his head thrown back and his hands held out as he prays aloud, while far across the empty pavement a second man in a red cloak stands alone with his head bowed and his hands pressed to his breast, but if we say, from men, they were afraid of the people, for they all held that john truly was a prophet, so they answered, we do not know, and jesus replied, neither will i tell you by what authority i am doing these things
pictures.name: pd_delen_pharisee_and_publican

lines.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples
and said to them, Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks, Why are you doing this? tell him, The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.
So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it,
and some who were standing there asked, Why are you untying the colt?
The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.
Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.
Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.
The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!
Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
The next day, when they had left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if there was any fruit on it. But when He reached it, He found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs.
Then He said to the tree, May no one ever eat of your fruit again. And His disciples heard this statement.

When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
And He would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.
Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, Is it not written: My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations? But you have made it a den of robbers.
When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him. For they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.
And when evening came, Jesus and His disciples went out of the city.
As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.
Peter remembered it and said, Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.
Have faith in God, Jesus said to them.
Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, Be lifted up and thrown into the sea, and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.
Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.
After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.
By what authority are You doing these things? they asked. And who gave You the authority to do them?
I will ask you one question, Jesus replied, and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
John's baptism, was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!
They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: If we say, From heaven, He will ask, Why then did you not believe him?
But if we say, From men, they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.
So they answered, We do not know. And Jesus replied, Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
